description: CR-001 Windows remainder (up.ps1/down.ps1/status.ps1 completed against CR-001 §5, the 6a shutdown blocker, the 6b User32 1074 task modelled on SpiralPool's BSD-3 wsl2-shutdown-hook.ps1, bootstrap install/-Uninstall/-Shortcuts, doctor checks, the full-stack SIGKILL crash-safety run), ossctl backup/restore with the Windows wrappers, and the five Phase 1 review round 6 NITs P1-15..P1-19 (phase2-plan.md items 21-25). The REAL shutdown/restart test of 6a/6b needs the user to restart the laptop and is done at the end of FEAT-011; this FEAT ships the code plus non-destructive live tests. Depends on FEAT-005..007 and FEAT-009 (backup include list needs the Hermes, skills and chat-attachment layout).
steps: Item 21: CR-001 §5 audit of scripts/up.ps1, scripts/down.ps1, scripts/status.ps1 and fix the gaps: status.ps1 shows on one screen lifecycle, kill, dry-run, running stages, pending approvals, outbox depth, last successful Telegram poll + reconnects, last shutdown type (graceful/hook/unclean from the boot-gate marker), the autostart/blocker/hook task states; down.ps1 and up.ps1 serialise on a per-user named mutex 'Local\ossbot-lifecycle' (decision: a second caller - e.g. 6a and 6b firing during the same shutdown - waits up to its own timeout, then exits 0 if the distro is already stopped), log to d:\Work\autonomous-oss-contributor\.ossbot-local\lifecycle.log, and keep PowerShell 5.1 compatibility (use the Invoke-OssWsl helpers). Live, non-destructive: down.ps1 -Timeout 10 -> status.ps1 -> up.ps1 -> status.ps1, record times.

Item 22: 6a shutdown blocker. Research first (record in a new docs/adr/00NN-windows-shutdown-hooks.md, NN = the next number not present in docs/adr at write time (0019 belongs to the CR-003 workflow)): WM_QUERYENDSESSION/WM_ENDSESSION, ShutdownBlockReasonCreate/Destroy requirements (top-level window, hidden or off-screen behaviour), the 5 s/'apps preventing shutdown' UI on Windows 11 26100, Fast Startup (HiberbootEnabled, read-only registry check) and whether WM_QUERYENDSESSION arrives on 'Shut down' with Fast Startup. Implement scripts/windows/ossbot-shutdown-blocker.ps1 (PowerShell 5.1, Add-Type C# compiled at runtime from source in the repo, no binary checked in, no copies to AppData): a top-level WinForms window (not shown in the taskbar; off-screen or hidden per the research) overriding WndProc; on WM_QUERYENDSESSION it calls ShutdownBlockReasonCreate('ossbot: stopping safely…'), runs scripts\down.ps1 -Timeout 90 (hard cap 90 + 90 s), then ShutdownBlockReasonDestroy and returns TRUE; single instance via a named mutex; logs to .ossbot-local\shutdown-blocker.log. Started at logon as a second action of the existing ossbot-autostart task (CR-001 wording) with ExecutionTimeLimit PT0S so Task Scheduler never kills it; kill.ps1 -Hard keeps disabling the task. Non-destructive live test tests\system\test_shutdown_blocker.ps1: start the blocker, find its window, SendMessage(WM_QUERYENDSESSION) to it, assert ShutdownBlockReasonQuery shows the reason while down runs, the distro ends stopped with shutdown type graceful, the reason is destroyed afterwards; then up.ps1.

Item 23: 6b event-triggered task 'ossbot-shutdown-hook' modelled on SpiralPool scripts/windows/wsl2-shutdown-hook.ps1 (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) 2026 Spiral Pool Contributors): per-user, non-elevated (RunLevel Limited, the logged-on user), trigger = event subscription System log, Provider User32, EventID 1074 only (NOT Kernel-Power 42 or any sleep event, unlike SpiralPool), action powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -File d:\Work\autonomous-oss-contributor\scripts\down.ps1 -Timeout 20 -Kind hook with ExecutionTimeLimit PT2M; script and log stay in the repo (no %APPDATA% helper copy, unlike SpiralPool). Verify a non-admin user can register a System-log event trigger on 26100; if not, record WARN in doctor and the ADR. If any SpiralPool code is adapted, keep its SPDX/copyright header in the adapted file and add a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md entry with the BSD-3 text; credit it in the shutdown-hooks ADR either way. Document that Windows does not wait for scheduled tasks (best effort). bootstrap.ps1: new phase 'shutdownhooks' installs 6a (autostart second action) and 6b, '-Uninstall' (new switch, reusing scripts\uninstall-host.ps1 logic) removes them and the autostart task, optional '-Shortcuts' creates Start-menu shortcuts 'ossbot Up/Down/Status/Kill' (off by default). ossctl.ps1 doctor checks the blocker process is running, the autostart second action and the hook task trigger XML match. Non-destructive live test: Start-ScheduledTask ossbot-shutdown-hook -> distro stops with shutdown type 'hook' -> up.ps1.

Item 24: crash safety and backup/restore. Run the full-stack SIGKILL e2e: tests/system/test_crash_safety.sh now covers gatekeeper, sandboxd, dockerfilter, runner (FEAT-006) and hermes (add it: SIGKILL ossbot-hermes mid-relay -> restart, relay re-gated by probe + surface check). Backup (DESIGN §18.8, ADR-0016): verify §23 item 26 (age release, sha256, 'age -d -i -' from stdin), pin age in config/versions.lock.yaml, install it in the apt-base step; src/ossbot/ctl/{backup.py,restore.py} (pause/checkpoint, SQLite online backup, audit verify on the copy, MANIFEST with sha256 per file, age-encrypted to profile.backup.age_recipients (refuse when empty), retention 8 in the gitignored d:\Work\autonomous-oss-contributor\backups\, include list = §18.8 + the Hermes state, active skills, feature stores and chat-attachment layout from the FEAT-007/009 findings; restore moves current state aside, forces killed + dry-run ON, invalidates approvals, re-applies chattr +a); ossctl 'backup [now]', 'backup schedule on|off', 'restore <archive>'; scripts/{backup.ps1,restore.ps1}; systemd/ossbot-backup.{service,timer} installed disabled. Tests: tests/unit/ctl/{test_backup.py,test_restore.py}, tests/system/test_backup_roundtrip.sh (in-place AC 22: audit verify passes, Hermes memory files identical, restored state killed + dry-run ON; the test resumes the system afterwards and uses a throwaway age identity under /root/.cache/ossbot-test, never the owner's).

Item 25: Phase 1 review round 6 NITs (docs/review-phase1.json): P1-15 add ::/128 (and ::ffff:0:0/96 as documentation) to always_denied.cidrs + squid goldens; P1-16 hyperv-firewall.ps1 requires exactly the two ossbot rules (Outbound, Allow, Enabled, TCP, 443/80) and re-creates drifted ones, ossctl.ps1 doctor validates properties and flags other Allow rules for the WSL VMCreatorId; P1-17 tests/unit/test_systemd_units.py asserts ProtectHome in {yes,tmpfs} for every non-root unit, test_egress_surface.sh and doctor assert Linger=no and no /run/user/<uid> for the five service uids, VERIFICATION threat-table row 41 updated; P1-18 reword threat-table rows 7/36 (research pool and Hermes hold a Kiro key + web_public; controls = ADR-0017 key out of tool reach + output key scans; CR-002 open adds agent-llm); P1-19 test_egress_surface.sh arms a root 'systemd-run --on-active=90' dead-man job restoring kernel.io_uring_disabled=2 and starting the watchdog timer before the sysctl write, cancelled after the restore. Then redeploy, run the FEAT verification, set status completed, write findings (blocker/hook observations, backup include list, anything the docs need), commit locally.
acceptance_criteria: status.ps1 shows every CR-001 §5 field; down/up serialise; the live down -> status -> up cycle is recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md

tests\system\test_shutdown_blocker.ps1 passes (WM_QUERYENDSESSION -> block reason set -> graceful down -> reason destroyed); Start-ScheduledTask ossbot-shutdown-hook brings the distro down with shutdown type 'hook'; bootstrap installs both, bootstrap -Uninstall removes both, ossctl.ps1 doctor checks both; the shutdown-hooks ADR records the research and credits SpiralPool
